note:
WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR. The v1 artifacts were retired once v2 became the single catalogue. Two things in them could not be re-derived, and both are here.

1. THE LEGACY CONTRACT HASHES. Every node the v1 contract described carried a contract_hash computed by an exporter that no longer exists, over a binary serialisation this repository cannot reproduce. Nothing in the runtime reads them -- the generated manifest carries only the current 'c2-' tokens -- but a graph or tool version pinned to one of these remains identifiable because the value survives here. They can never be recomputed, so they are kept rather than dropped.

2. THE ANTI-DELETION GUARD. `gen_artifacts.py --continuity` asserts that every function name and every card id listed here is still present in the live catalogue. That is the guarantee the old --roundtrip provided, at 1 per cent of the weight: it proves nothing that once existed has silently disappeared, without keeping 4.5 MB of superseded artifacts to compare against.

GROWTH IS EXPECTED, LOSS IS NOT. The catalogue is larger than this file and will keep growing; --continuity checks one direction only.

3. THE DECLARED CATEGORY RENAMES. A rename is not a loss, but it looks like one to any membership check, so it is declared here with its date and its reason where a reviewer sees it -- never by relaxing the check. This block replaced corpus/_renames.json, which lost its only reader when the round-trip was retired.
